speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing weakness and fatigue; to help me diagnose the cause, please tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if they occur more during the day or at rest.

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. Given your recent travel, hiking, camping, and history of multiple illnesses, I need to clarify your current medication list and any specific infections you've had, as well as ask if you have experienced unexplained weight loss or fever recently.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, TSH, and Creatine Kinase.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history provided. Social history: Enjoys outdoor activities such as hiking and camping. No mention of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, headache, or any respiratory, gastrointestinal, or urinary symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (formerly ME/CFS).

While your previous provider suggested a Urinary Tract Infection, you explicitly deny fever, dysuria, or urinary symptoms, and you also deny respiratory or gastrointestinal issues. Given your recent hiking/camping, multiple recent illnesses, and profound fatigue worsening by the end of the day that impacts self-care, this clinical picture aligns more closely with Post-Viral Fatigue Syndrome or Chronic Fatigue Syndrome rather than an active UTI.
